sources: SATURDAY Oct 31 2026 RUN, markets closed. Carries FRIDAY Oct 30 closes for VIX, Brent, DXY, gold, copper and the curve, plus FRED prints through Oct 28-29. HEADLINE: RISK VOL ARRIVED ON FRIDAY, BUT IT CAME FROM THE AI COMPLEX AND FROM OIL, NOT FROM THE MACRO BOARD. VOL - VIX JUMPED TO 19.42 ON THE OCT 30 CLOSE, PLUS 12.9 PCT FROM 17.20, with an intraday high of 22.31, the highest since April. Against 19.45 on Oct 23 the tile is FLAT on the week, so this is a round trip to last Friday level rather than a new vol regime - but it is the single biggest daily move on the board. The driver is AI capex: Nasdaq minus 2.9 pct (worst day since June 5), S&P 500 minus 1.8 pct to 7,580.07, Dow minus 1.1 pct. Amazon fell about 2 pct on a record negative 42 bn USD twelve-month free cash flow, Alphabet kept sliding after Thursday earnings miss (its worst day in over 20 years), Intel fell about 26-29 pct on a weak Q4 outlook. Meta and Alphabet are now more than 20 pct off their 52-week highs, Tesla minus 19 pct, Amazon minus 15 pct, Nvidia minus 12 pct. October: Nasdaq minus about 5 pct, its worst month since March 2025. Separately a roughly 6.3 bn USD Binance hack, the largest crypto theft on record, took bitcoin down about 5 pct to around 76,600 USD. OIL - NEW HIGHS, AND A CONTRACT ROLL THAT MAKES THE TILE LOOK LOWER THAN IT IS. READ THIS BEFORE READING THE BRENT TILE: the December contract EXPIRED Friday at 117.64 USD, plus 2.76, after touching 118 intraday; the JANUARY contract is now front month and settled at 113.43 USD, plus 2.63. The tile carries 113.43, so the roll alone takes about 4 USD off the headline number. Brent did NOT fall on Friday, it rose, and it is plus 13.6 pct on the month from a start near 100-102 USD. WTI 104.12, plus 2.12. Against 111.70 on Oct 23 the tile is UP. AND THE SUPPLY STORY HAS FINALLY PRODUCED A CONFIRMED EVENT: UKMTO reported on Friday a tanker struck by explosive devices attached by a small boat, which maritime sources call the FIRST KNOWN SUCCESSFUL LIMPET-MINE STRIKE in the waterway since February; the attacker is unidentified. Iran Revolutionary Guards claimed Thursday that tankers hit mines on a southern route, which US Central Command rejected, saying main transit routes were cleared. An armed group shut a valve on Libya Hamada pipeline, halting about 15,000 b/d. The Houthi claims on Ras Tanura, Rabigh and Abqaiq remain UNCONFIRMED by Riyadh for a THIRTEENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN - a Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a cruise missile. Reports say the US may resume strikes on Iran, with action reportedly signalled for after the midterms. The US has had non-emergency government staff leaving Saudi Arabia since Oct 23. OPEC+ seven core members meet online SUNDAY NOV 1 and three Reuters sources expect December targets held, with no final decision made. CURVE - THE STEEPENING KEEPS BUILDING. FRED T10Y2Y Oct 30 at 0.38, a new high for the move (0.37 Oct 29, 0.38 Oct 28, 0.29 Oct 27, 0.32 Oct 26). Against 0.31 on Oct 23 that is PLUS 7bp, tile UP for a second run. The 10-year sits around 4.93 pct and rising borrowing costs were cited as a direct cause of the tech selloff. This is the transmission channel to watch: term premium is now expensive enough to hurt long-duration equity. BREAKEVEN - STILL UP ON THE WEEK, DOWN ON THE DAY. FRED T5YIFR Oct 29 at 2.23 pct, giving back 4bp from 2.27 but still plus 3bp against 2.20 on Oct 23, so the tile stays UP for a second run. FED - TWO MORE HAWKS SPEAK. After the split hold this week, Musalem (St Louis) and Barkin (Richmond) both said rates need to rise further. With September core PCE at 3.1 pct and rising, expectations for a DECEMBER HIKE firmed. The Bank of Japan held at 1.25 pct and the yen firmed. CREDIT - FIRST WIDENING IN FOUR RUNS, BUT STILL INSIDE LAST WEEK. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 Oct 29 at 3.26 pct, 12bp WIDER than the 3.14 October tight (3.18 Oct 27, 3.30 Oct 26, 3.38 Oct 23). Tile 314 to 326bp. Against 338bp a week ago that is still minus 12bp so the trend tile remains DOWN, but the direction of travel flipped on Thursday and this is the first credit tile to move with the equity selloff. Oct 30 had not posted at run time - re-read next run, because if HY keeps widening while VIX holds above 19 the Oct 22-23 scare is reopening. METALS - COPPER-GOLD MAKES A SIXTH CONSECUTIVE NEW HIGH ON A VIOLENT GOLD SELLOFF. Gold 3,875.84 USD/t.oz MINUS 3.62 pct, minus 145.47 USD on the day, now decisively through 4,000; copper 6.4585 USD/Lbs minus 1.86 pct. Copper-gold 6.4585/3875.84*1000 = 1.6663, tile 1.65 to 1.67, up from 1.57 a week ago. Trend UP. BUT NOTE THE COMPOSITION WARNING, NOW LOUDER THAN LAST RUN: copper FELL too. This is not copper leading, it is gold collapsing faster, i.e. the safety bid unwinding into a hawkish Fed and a 4.93 pct ten-year. A gold-driven copper-gold high is a WEAKER pro-growth signal than a copper-driven one, and on a day when equities fell 1.8 pct it should not be read as risk appetite. DOLLAR - FLAT FOR A SECOND RUN, AND IT IS NOW A GENUINE PUZZLE. DXY 101.879 minus 0.15 pct, against 101.79 a week ago, so plus 0.09 pct and the tile stays FLAT. Hot Q3 GDP, re-accelerating core PCE, two hike dissents, two more hawkish regional presidents and a 4.93 pct ten-year have bought the dollar nothing in three sessions. Either the dollar is wrong or the hike pricing is. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - CARRIED, STILL EASY. NFCI minus 0.487 for the week ending OCT 23 (minus 0.494 Oct 16, minus 0.501 Oct 9, minus 0.508 Oct 2). Tile minus 0.49, FLAT. Next update NOV 4, which will be the first NFCI to contain any of Friday vol. GLOBAL LIQUIDITY - STILL 1 (STABLE), AND THE OCT 28 H.4.1 HAS NOW LANDED. FRED WALCL Oct 28 at 6,745,635 million USD, MINUS 7,969 million on the week (6,753,604 Oct 21, 6,755,639 Oct 14, 6,747,560 Oct 7). That is a slightly faster drain than the prior week minus 2,035 million but far too small to be a regime change; no change at the ECB, PBOC or BOJ. Tile 1. Next WALCL NOV 5. LABOUR - CARRIED, NO NEW PRINT. Initial claims 194k for the week ending OCT 24 (195k Oct 17, 200k Oct 10, 198k Oct 3), FRED page last updated Oct 29. Against 195k a week ago the tile goes from DOWN to FLAT. Next print THURSDAY NOV 5. No labour-market crack. MACRO TILES - ALL CARRIED. ISM Manufacturing 54.5 September, NEXT PRINT MONDAY NOV 2. Consumer sentiment 48.0, UMich October final, a five-month low. Building permits 1,398k SAAR September (revised). Sahm Rule 0.00 September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50. LEI y/y plus 1.2 pct carried and LOW PRECISION - the Oct 22 Conference Board release has the index unchanged at 99.6 and publishes no y/y figure. All FLAT. BLIND SPOTS - MOVE IS NOW THE EXPENSIVE ONE. The MOVE index is CARRIED at 103.31 for OCT 23 for a SIXTEENTH consecutive run: Investing.com still stops at Oct 23 (106.84 Oct 22, 95.94 Oct 21, 101.70 Oct 20, 101.30 Oct 19, 101.10 Oct 16), CNBC and MacroMicro both failed to serve. TREAT THE MOVE TILE AS BLIND, NOT AS CALM - it is held FLAT by default on the exact run where equity vol jumped 13 pct, the ten-year is at 4.93 pct and a December hike is being priced. Rate vol is the one thing that would tell us whether Friday was an equity event or a rates event, and we cannot see it. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread is a STANDING ASSUMPTION at 0bp and the EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis a STANDING ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp, not measurements; every free source serves a SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread. Scorecard unchanged: two assumed tiles, one judgement tile (global liquidity), one stale tile (MOVE), one low-precision carry (LEI) out of eighteen. CALENDAR: OPEC+ SUNDAY NOV 1. ISM Manufacturing MONDAY NOV 2. US MIDTERMS TUESDAY NOV 3. NFCI NOV 4. WALCL and jobless claims NOV 5. Sahm NOV 6. October CPI mid-November. Next FOMC December. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD c4cf644, the Oct 30 commit); this scheduled session remains the SOLE writer of data.json; the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17; BDTI stays removed since Oct 17. The .git lock-file pile keeps growing because this session cannot delete files in the folder - still harmless, but it WILL eventually break a git operation, and clearing it needs delete permission on the Dashboard Macro folder. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, SIXTEENTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in PLAIN TEXT in .git/config; fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Untracked junk still in the repo root: _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: the macro board is UNCHANGED AND STILL REFLATIONARY - growth hot, labour fine, conditions easy, credit inside last week, curve steepening, copper-gold at a new high - while the PRICE side has started to crack in two specific places: the AI complex and the Gulf. Friday was not a macro repricing. It was a 13 pct VIX day driven by AI capex disappointments and a 4.93 pct ten-year, landing on a board where nothing recessionary is visible. The three live threats into next week are a confirmed hit on Saudi crude infrastructure (now one step closer after the first successful limpet-mine strike), an ISM miss MONDAY after a 3.4 pct GDP print, and the MIDTERMS TUESDAY. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: whether HY keeps widening from 326bp, which is the single cleanest test of whether Friday was contagion or a tech reset; ISM Monday; the midterms Tuesday and the reported post-midterm Iran decision; OPEC+ Sunday; getting a live MOVE print; whether gold keeps collapsing or the safety bid returns; whether the dollar ever responds to hot US data; rotating the embedded PAT; clearing the .git lock files.
